name.description:
The name of the library, e.g. 'pandas', 'lunar'.

Optionally, the version of the library can be specified in the library name. When the version is included, it
should be formatted according to the library's #packageManager.
   e.g. "pandas=4.2.0" for conda or "pandas==4.2.0" for pip or "react@18.3.1"

For NPM, an optional alias can be specified at the beginning, separated by @.
   e.g. "react16@react@16.14.0" for react to be aliased as react16 with version 16.14.0

installationUrl.description:
In rare cases, a package can only be installed using a full URL rather than just the package manager and library
name. For example, a pip package hosted in a private customer repository may only be available via the full URL
(though configuring a private conda or pip repo would be preferable). In these cases, #name should be the library's
(importable) name and `installationUrl` should be set to the full URL used during package installation.

e.g. `name`: `my-package`,
     `installationUrl`: `https://github.com/my_org/my_repo/releases/download/my_package-0.1.tar.gz`

packageManager.description:
The package manager required to install this library.

**NOTE:** For Python packages, `conda` is strongly preferred to `pip` as a package manager for C3 runtimes.

title:
A Library represents one or more language-specific modules necessary for executing in a given
{@link ImplLanguage.Runtime}.
name: ImplLanguage.Library
